notes.meaning: The Lord invites Noah and his family to enter the ark because He saw Noah living faithfully in a corrupt world. To be righteous before God means to be accepted by Him through faith, not by earning it through human perfection. God treated Noah with the care of a loving father who calls his children indoors before a violent storm begins.

God commands Noah to bring seven pairs of each clean animal and bird, but only one pair of each unclean kind. The clean animals were suitable for worship sacrifices and would later serve as food for mankind. By providing extra clean animals, God made sure that true worship would continue on earth after the disaster.

God gives a final warning that heavy rain will fall for forty days and nights, beginning in just seven days, to wipe out all land life. This one-week delay gave the watching world one final chance to turn back to God, but people ignored it. In Scripture, forty days often marks a solemn season of testing and divine judgment.
Noah obeyed every detail of what the Lord commanded him to do. He did not pick and choose which instructions were easy, but showed complete trust through steady obedience.
Noah was six hundred years old when the great flood came upon the earth. Even in his advanced old age and after over a century of patient building, his faith in God did not fail.

Noah entered the ark alongside his wife, his three sons, and their wives to find refuge from the rising waters. Each son took only one wife, honoring God's original pattern for marriage as they prepared to restart the human race.

Pairs of clean and unclean animals, birds, and crawling creatures came directly to Noah and entered the ark just as God had ordered. Noah did not need to hunt or capture these wild beasts himself. God placed a quiet impulse within the creatures so they gathered peacefully into their shelter.
The floodwaters began to rise on the earth exactly seven days after God had spoken. Noah and his family had to sit in the ark for a full week by faith before seeing any rain fall.

On the seventeenth day of the second month, massive underground reservoirs burst open while torrential rain poured from the sky. The natural boundaries God set at creation were removed so water could overwhelm the land from both below and above. This exact date marks the historical reality of the great catastrophe.
A violent downpour fell over the entire earth without stopping for forty days and forty nights. This was not normal rain, but an unending torrent that steadily drowned the dry land.

The text repeats the exact entrance of Noah, his family, and every kind of living creature into the ark on that very day. This repetition emphasizes how completely God kept His promise to save them. Every kind of land animal created in the beginning was safely sheltered to start the world anew.
Creatures of every kind that breathe air came in pairs to Noah and boarded the ship. God's miraculous power kept wild and tame animals resting quietly together without harming one another.

After the animals and family had entered, the Lord Himself sealed the door of the ark shut. God closed the door to keep Noah perfectly safe from the raging waters, and to shut out a rebellious world whose time for repentance was over. Our eternal safety rests in God's hands rather than our own strength.

As the floodwaters grew deeper over the forty days, they lifted the ark high above the ground. The very waters that destroyed everything else carried the ark to safety. Trouble that ruins the ungodly often lifts God's people closer to Him.

The flood surged with tremendous power across the land, and the ark floated smoothly upon the surface of the deep. While all human buildings collapsed beneath the surge, God's chosen vessel stayed afloat.

The waters rose so high that every mountain under heaven was covered, rising more than twenty feet above the highest peaks. No sinner could escape God's reach by fleeing to high ground. The ark alone rode safely above the covered mountains under God's watchful care.

differ.view: The flood covered the whole region where early mankind lived rather than the entire globe, using language describing the observer's complete horizon.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Scripture does not require the deluge to be geographically worldwide, provided that all of early humanity outside the ark perished.

notes.meaning: Every living land creature—birds, livestock, wild animals, swarming things, and all of mankind—perished in the flood. Only creatures that breathed air on dry ground died; sea creatures were not destroyed in this way. When human beings fell into sin, the animal creation under their care shared in the earthly consequences.

God wiped out every living creature from the earth, leaving alive only Noah and those with him in the ark. This terrible event showed that God's warnings about the wages of sin always come true. Noah was spared because he had separated himself from the wickedness of the world to follow God alone.

The floodwaters stayed at their full height upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days, which was about five months. This long period demonstrated God's serious anger against sin and allowed the corrupted earth to be cleansed. Throughout those long months, God faithfully preserved Noah and his household inside the ark.
